citation: Sumi Y, Nakayama C, Kadotani H, Matsuo M, Ozeki Y, Kinoshita T, et al. Resting Heart Rate Variability Is Associated With Subsequent Orthostatic Hypotension: Comparison Between Healthy Older People and Patients With Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder. Front Neurol. 2020;11:567984.
protocol: Orthostatic challenge: 15 min supine, then 15 min standing. Baseline BP and pulse rate are taken in the supine position before standing; delta values at 1 and 3 min after standing.
population: 42 healthy older controls (16 male, 26 female), age 70.2 +/- 6.6 y, BMI 22.4 +/- 3.0; comorbidities are printed (some hypertension, diabetes and coronary disease) despite the healthy label.
note: Baseline is the supine value before standing. Methods give mean +/- SD for parametric variables, which applies to these cells. The control group has a non-trivial comorbidity load, so the healthy label is the authors' own.
